subject.title: [Feature]: Telegram — full agent activity visibility (Web UI parity)

question: Should OpenClaw add a default-off persistent Telegram activity mode, and what disclosure, redaction, retention, NO_REPLY/internal-turn, and message-volume policy should protect reasoning and tool telemetry?
rationale: The source gap is real, but implementing it changes third-party chat disclosure and retention semantics and likely adds public config surface rather than repairing a narrow broken path.

options.title: Add guarded Telegram activity mode
options.body: Implement a default-off mode with redacted summaries, bounded message volume, NO_REPLY/internal-turn exclusions, docs, focused tests, and live Telegram proof.

options.title: Keep current Telegram visibility model
options.body: Document preview/progress plus /verbose and /reasoning as the intended Telegram debug behavior and close or narrow this direction after maintainer confirmation.

options.title: Keep durable detail outside Telegram
options.body: Direct durable activity inspection to Control UI or another approved observer surface instead of retaining detailed telemetry in Telegram chat history.

recommendation.title: Add guarded Telegram activity mode
recommendation.body: Implement a default-off mode with redacted summaries, bounded message volume, NO_REPLY/internal-turn exclusions, docs, focused tests, and live Telegram proof.

likelyOwner.reason: This spans Telegram channel UX, shared streaming config, and security defaults, and steipete has the strongest adjacent product/history signal in this review.
